title: Emergency stabilization: prevent cascading 5xx and timeout amplification during customer replay storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise customers experienced repeat 5xx waves and long-tail timeouts during replayed upload/ingest traffic. Root cause appears to be a regression in connection reuse and hidden client-side retries that amplify bursts, causing connection-pool starvation in the edge proxy and mid-flight TCP/TLS resets. This ticket scopes a minimal, backward-compatible stabilization: short-term patches in edge-proxy and SDK guidance, and a medium-term plan to add per-tenant adaptive retry dampening and early circuit warmup to prevent future amplification.
regression_cause: Edge-proxy changed KeepAlive/connection_reuse semantics in 2.4.0 -> unintended connection churn under high short-lived request rates; SDKs with aggressive retry defaults (no idempotency token) replayed requests which could trigger duplicate in-flight work and queue pressure. Combination led to connection exhaustion and cascading 5xx/timeouts.
mitigation_plan: Hotpatch edge-proxy: increase connection pool headroom for short-lived clients and restore previous keepalive timeout (PR linked)
Disable/soft-limit automatic client retries when idempotency token missing via runtime header shim
Deploy tenant-scoped request leaky-bucket at edge to limit instantaneous inflight requests
Add quick telemetry: per-tenant inflight-count, retry-count, and connection-reset-rate dashboards
rollout_plan: Canary hotpatch to 10% of frontdoors in us-east-1 for 1 hour (obs smoke tests) -> expand to 50% -> global
Ship simultaneous SDK advisory and default config change to SDKs (node/python) to avoid blind replay
If canary shows no amplification after 30m, proceed full rollout; otherwise abort and roll back
Coordinate with Dedicated & Private channels: provide ops runbook + one-line config change for customers not on hosted
updates: 2026-03-12: Incident reported by two enterprise customers; support escalated to eng. Initial triage indicates high retry counts and connection resets in edge logs.
2026-03-12: Added emergency observability panels (inflight requests, retry amplification, connection reset rate). Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-infra/show/tenant-replay-storm
2026-03-13: Reproduced locally with replay harness. Confirmed edge-proxy keepalive regression increases connection churn under short-lived upload patterns.
2026-03-14: Implemented runtime header shim to mark requests without idempotency token; SDK advisory prepared (PRs: node#823, python#410).
2026-03-15: Canary begun (us-east-1 10% frontdoors). Monitoring shows 70% reduction in connection resets and lower 5xx rate for affected tenants. Continuing rollout after 60m observation window.
observability: Trace: sample trace showing mid-flight connection reset https://traces.redwood.svc/trace/0a1b2c
Logs: edge-proxy connection_reset spikes filter query: service=edge-proxy levels=error tag=conn_reset
acceptance_criteria: Post-rollout, affected tenants show sustained 90% reduction in 5xx spikes attributable to connection resets for 24h
Client-visible retry amplification metric drops below threshold (per-tenant retry amplification < 1.5x)
Dedicated/Private customers have clear config diff and runbook delivered; at least 2 ops-contacts verified in staging
Regression added to CI fuzz harness to catch keepalive/connection reuse regressions
customer_comms: 2026-03-12: Initial acknowledgement sent to customers; we are triaging and will provide hourly updates
2026-03-13: Notified customers of planned temporary SDK guidance and edge hotpatch window
2026-03-15: Post-canya confirmation to affected customers; suggested SDK config changes and provided detailed incident summary link
postmortem_actions: 1) Add CI regression tests for connection reuse patterns in edge-proxy
2) Default SDK retry backoff to conservative for non-idempotent requests and document idempotency token best practices
3) Implement per-tenant adaptive retry dampening (follow-up ticket) and per-tenant surge budget telemetry
4) Improve runbook to include fast rollback steps and customer-facing communications template
notes: Trade-offs: increasing pool headroom reduces headroom for other tenants in extreme scenarios; mitigated by per-tenant leaky bucket and circuit warmup approach
Long-term: explore request-fingerprinting at edge to deduplicate replays before backend execution
Coordination: inform Dedicated/Private release engineers to prepare identical config toggle for on-prem and VPC deployments
